title: `atan2(0, 0)`
verdict: no option matches: 0, where the reference raises
description: `atan2(0.0, 0.0)` is 0. With signed zeros it is C's `std::atan2`, which `ieee_floating_point_ops` does not change: `atan2(-0.0::DOUBLE, -0.0::DOUBLE)` is -π (-3.141592653589793). sverify's SQL normalizes `-0.0` to `0.0` on every read (duckdb-R14). (Corrected 2026-11-04: this said `atan2(0, 0)` is 0 for every zero.)

With `ieee_floating_point_ops` off, a zero divisor of doubles raises, and so do the elementary functions outside their domains (as the reference does), and `power(0, negative)` raises; the NaN of `inf - inf`, `0 * inf` and `inf / inf`, `atan2(0, 0)` and the shifts are unchanged.
The docs are silent on `atan2` of zeros: a docs gap. No upstream test pins this; it may change between versions.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe` runs the function at each signature on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the 64-bit bounds, 0.5, ±2.5, 1e308, ±inf, NaN, NULL), one row at a time from columns, under every combination of `error_on_division_by_zero` and `ieee_floating_point_ops`. Lean evaluates the Substrait call on the same rows once per candidate value of its option (`substrait-check --outcomes`), and the candidates whose outcomes all match are DuckDB's options. No input is -0.0 (duckdb-R14).

evidence.note: ATan2: std::atan2 on doubles; not bound through BindIEEEFloating, so the setting does not change it

provenance.notes: Corrected the description: `atan2(0, 0)` is 0 for +0, +0 only; `atan2(-0.0, -0.0)` is -π.
